raw_segments.text: Then you can imagine the times that he had with his companions, ducking under the rollers,
or coming in on top of a comer, and landing with a swash and a splutter as the big wave
went whirling far up the beach, or standing up on his tail and scratching his head as
the old people did, or playing, I'm the king of the castle, on slippery, weedy rocks
that just stuck out of the wash.
Now and then he would see a thin fin, like a big shark's fin, drifting along close
to shore, and he knew that that was the killer whale, the grandpus, who eats young seals
when he can get them, and Kodak would head for the beach like an arrow, and the fin would
jig off slowly, as if it were looking for nothing at all.
